profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting at a university-affiliated hospital research unit to finalize the workplan for a grant proposal on using Value of Information (VOI) to shape a pragmatic phase III trial in relapsed atrial fibrillation. The team has already agreed in principle to propose a trial comparing a new ablation workflow against current care, and this meeting is to map out what analyses will be done, who will prepare them, and what timeline will support a submission to the hospital's internal funding board next Thursday. The agenda is to align on the comparator set to be represented in the VOI model, define what the 'base-case' and 'final recommendation' outputs will include, assign responsibility for drafting the trial design section versus the economic modeling appendix, and confirm what needs to be ready for the Monday pre-review. The expected outcome is a shared plan for the proposal package, including analysis deliverables, ownership, and deadlines.

members.name: Dr. Maya Srinivasan
members.role: Consultant Electrophysiologist and Clinical Trial Lead
members.expertise: Cardiac rhythm management, multicenter trial operations, pragmatic trial design
members.background: Maya is a senior clinician who has led device and ablation studies across NHS partner sites and often translates methodological work into fundable clinical protocols.
members.private_state: She wants a clean, fundable protocol that reviewers will see as operationally realistic, and she is quietly worried that too many modeled options will make the trial seem unfocused or politically difficult across sites that already use different pathways.
hidden_assumptions: When discussing 'relevant comparators,' only treatments that most participating sites could plausibly randomize between in the proposed trial need to be carried through planning materials.
The 'current pathway' can be represented as a single usual-care arm even if, in practice, usual care contains several treatment variants used across hospitals.
For the Monday pre-review, a 'base-case model' means a sufficiently polished clinical-economic narrative with headline outputs, not a fully parameterized model including every low-uptake option.
Once trial data are available, options not directly randomized would normally fall out of the main recommendation framework unless they are central to the protocol.

members.name: Dr. Leon Weber
members.role: Health Economist and Decision Modeling Lead
members.expertise: Cost-effectiveness modeling, VOI analysis, trial design for reimbursement decisions
members.background: Leon is a health economist with experience advising NICE-style evidence development programs and specializes in how comparator structure affects EVPI and EVPPI estimates.
members.private_state: He wants methodological integrity preserved in the proposal because he knows reviewers in health economics will reject a VOI-led design if the decision model collapses feasible alternatives too early, and he is concerned the clinical team will unintentionally narrow the decision problem.
hidden_assumptions: When discussing 'relevant comparators,' all clinically feasible options that could affect the adoption decision in the target health system must remain in the VOI model, whether or not they are randomized in the trial.

The 'current pathway' is not a single arm for modeling purposes if rate-control optimization, antiarrhythmic drug escalation, and conventional ablation remain distinct feasible choices with different costs and outcomes.
A 'base-case model' for internal review should already contain the full comparator set and working parameterization, even if some evidence inputs are provisional.

The 'final recommendation' after data collection still requires evaluating all retained comparators in the updated decision model, including non-randomized alternatives fed by prior or external evidence.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the proposal should consider 'all relevant comparators.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the trial planning documents should include the interventions that are realistic contenders for randomization across participating sites: the new ablation workflow and a broad usual-care alternative.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the VOI decision model must include every feasible management option that could alter the eventual treatment recommendation, including antiarrhythmic escalation and standard ablation pathways even if they are not randomized.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds methodologically standard and both sincerely endorse it, so neither expects the other to attach a different boundary to the word 'relevant'; the divergence hides inside what counts as relevant rather than whether comparators matter.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to modeling or comparing against the 'current pathway' or 'usual care.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this is one aggregate comparator arm that pragmatically bundles existing site-specific management patterns into a single current-care category.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes 'current pathway' is only a shorthand label in conversation and will later be unpacked into several separate comparators because aggregation would distort VOI and downstream recommendations.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In clinical planning meetings, 'usual care' is a common convenience phrase, and because both are focused on moving the plan forward, neither pauses to ask whether it is a single modeled option or a placeholder for multiple branches.

misalignment_points.topic: What needs to be ready for the 'base-case' by Monday
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that Leon will circulate the 'base-case' before the Monday pre-review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes a base-case means a review-ready summary with headline ICER and VOI outputs for the proposed comparison, enough to anchor the grant narrative and show feasibility.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes a base-case means an operational model run with the full comparator structure and provisional evidence synthesis, because otherwise the VOI outputs are not interpretable for design choices.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are accustomed to using 'base-case' as a routine milestone term, and the meeting concerns planning rather than technical inspection, so they assume shared standards without spelling out what minimum completeness the milestone implies.

misalignment_points.topic: What happens at the recommendation stage
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the model should support the 'final recommendation' once trial data come in.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes the final recommendation will be between the trial arms, with any other options treated as background context rather than live contenders in the updated decision.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes the post-trial recommendation must still compare all retained feasible options in the decision model, combining trial results with outside evidence for non-randomized comparators.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They both speak as though the recommendation phase is already conceptually settled, but each imports a different default from their discipline: clinicians think in terms of protocol arms, while health economists think in terms of the full reimbursement decision set.

turns.inner_thought: We need something the internal board can back without seeing a sprawling methodological exercise. The cleanest story is still the new ablation workflow against a single current pathway, framed as pragmatic and deliverable across sites with different routines. If we start proliferating branches now, the protocol will look messy and politically awkward.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making time. I think the main thing today is to get a fundable VOI-led story into shape for next week's board. We already have agreement in principle on the new ablation workflow versus the current pathway, so if we can keep the narrative clear and operational, we should be in good shape.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, but only if the economics side doesn't quietly narrow the decision problem. For VOI to mean anything to reviewers, all relevant comparators need to stay in the model from the start, not just the trial arms. Otherwise the uncertainty analysis will be answering the wrong question.
turns.utterance: I agree. From my side, I just want to make sure the proposal is explicit that we're considering all relevant comparators, so the VOI piece is genuinely informing the design rather than just decorating it.

turns.inner_thought: That should be easy enough: the protocol can stay as two practical arms, and Leon can describe the current pathway in the appendix in whatever modeling language he needs, as long as the board sees a straightforward trial and the final recommendation is anchored to the randomized comparison.
turns.utterance: That makes sense. What I'd suggest is that the protocol section stays focused on the two practical arms, and then in your appendix you can show how the current pathway is handled in the model. That way the main document stays readable, but we still show the decision logic that supports the final recommendation.

turns.inner_thought: Two arms in the protocol is fine, as long as nobody assumes that means two options in the model. Once the base-case is built with the full comparator structure, I can quantify where uncertainty sits across the relevant options and use that to justify what the trial should and should not measure.
turns.utterance: Yes, that's fine with me. Once we have the base-case in place, we can also see how much value there is in reducing uncertainty across the relevant options, which should help us justify the design choices quite cleanly.

turns.inner_thought: Good. If he can get me a polished base-case with the key outputs by Monday, the investigators can react to something concrete and we can tighten the grant language before Thursday. I don't need every technical detail nailed down for that meeting, just something review-ready.
turns.utterance: Perfect. Could you circulate the base-case by Monday? I'd like the clinical investigators to have the headline outputs in hand before the pre-review so we can test whether the story lands.

turns.inner_thought: Monday is doable if I push the evidence inputs over the weekend. I should make clear, at least in broad terms, that the base-case retains antiarrhythmic escalation, the conventional ablation route, and the new workflow as distinct options for the decision analysis. That is the minimum defensible structure.
turns.utterance: Monday is workable. I'll structure the base-case so that antiarrhythmic escalation, the conventional ablation route, and the new workflow are all retained for the decision analysis, and then we can see what that means for the overall case.

turns.inner_thought: Fine, as long as that sits in the appendix and doesn't muddy the proposal's front-end message. Reviewers need to read this as a simple comparison against usual care, not as a negotiation over every local variation in practice.
turns.utterance: That sounds sensible. As long as the proposal still reads as a straightforward comparison against usual care, I think reviewers will be comfortable with it.

turns.inner_thought: Exactly—clear on the surface, but methodologically intact underneath. If we preserve the comparator set now, we won't have to rebuild the decision problem later, and the final recommendation after the trial can still be made on the right basis.
turns.utterance: Yes, that should work. And keeping the comparator set intact now will matter later as well, because the model needs to support the final recommendation once the trial reads out.

turns.inner_thought: Right—the whole point is to tell sites whether the new workflow should replace the existing pathway they currently deliver. If that message gets diluted, the proposal loses clinical traction.
turns.utterance: Exactly. In the end they'll want a clear recommendation on whether sites should adopt the new workflow over the existing pathway, so the line of sight needs to stay obvious all the way through.

turns.inner_thought: I should head off any concern from the economics reviewers by briefly explaining why all relevant comparators remain in the model even though the trial schema itself is simpler. That usually reassures people that the VOI is being used properly.
turns.utterance: I'll draft a short note on that for the appendix—just explaining why all relevant comparators stay in the model even if only two arms appear in the trial schema.

turns.inner_thought: Good. He can own the technical appendix; I'll keep the protocol narrative disciplined around recruitment, site delivery, and a practical usual-care comparator. That's the package the board will actually read.
turns.utterance: Great. Why don't you take the modeling appendix and that rationale note, and I'll draft the protocol narrative around recruitment, sites, and the practical usual-care comparator for Thursday's board pack.

turns.inner_thought: That division works. I need to deliver an actual working base-case, not just slides, plus a short explanation of the comparator logic and a section on how the model will feed through to the eventual recommendation. If I get that over by Monday, we can still refine presentation before Thursday.
turns.utterance: That works for me. I'll send the base-case on Monday, along with the comparator rationale note and a draft section on how the model supports the eventual recommendation, and then we can tighten the wording after the pre-review.
